summary: The weekly criminal filings report has been re-run and now lists all seven Fairbanks court files that were missing from the previous run; all seven carried numbers above the end of that report's series, which corrects what this record reported on Oct. 20. The new report lists 43 cases filed at Fairbanks between Oct. 14 and Oct. 20 and no filings at all for Monday, Oct. 19, the second consecutive report whose window covers that day and lists nothing. A Nenana case carries an indicted first-degree burglary charge, a Class B felony, and a second Nenana case charges three Class C felony assault counts; both charge lists had to be expanded in the database before the full counts could be read. A North Pole man was arrested on a domestic violence assault charge late on Oct. 20 and no court file exists yet. The weekly dispositions report has not been refreshed since Oct. 19 and its window still reaches only that date, so no closures after Oct. 15 appear in it. The U.S. Attorney's press index for the District of Alaska could not be read: the direct route was refused and the only route that answers has not published anything since Aug. 27.

entries.title: North Pole man arrested on a domestic violence assault charge
body: The Alaska State Troopers report that at about 8:59 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 20 they received a report of a domestic violence assault in North Pole, and that Christopher Reynolds, 50, of North Pole, was arrested and taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center on one charge of domestic violence assault in the fourth degree. The entry was posted at 12:23 a.m. on Oct. 21.

No court file has been opened in the case. A search of the public case database for filings under that name between Oct. 1 and Oct. 21 returns no records, and no case has been filed at the Fairbanks courthouse above 4FA-26-02124CR. The charge described is the one recorded by police; no charge classification is given here because no court file states one.
He is arrested, not convicted. No victim is identified.

sources.label: Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, Oct. 21

entries.title: Weekly criminal filings: 43 cases at Fairbanks, and the seven files missing from last week's report now appear in it
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal charges filed, run at 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 20 and covering Oct. 14 to Oct. 20, records 43 cases filed at the Fairbanks courthouse and two at Delta Junction. It records no cases at Nenana and none at Healy. The report runs to 68 pages.

The Fairbanks cases run in an unbroken series from 4FA-26-02082CR to 4FA-26-02124CR. By filing day they are: Wednesday eight, Thursday three, Friday fourteen, Saturday six, Sunday nine and Tuesday three.

All seven Fairbanks files that the previous report did not list now appear in it: 4FA-26-02118CR and 4FA-26-02121CR under Friday, Oct. 16; 4FA-26-02120CR and 4FA-26-02122CR under Saturday, Oct. 17; and 4FA-26-02119CR, 4FA-26-02123CR and 4FA-26-02124CR under Tuesday, Oct. 20.

Each of those seven carries a number above 4FA-26-02117CR, which was the highest number the previous report listed, so they were absent from above the end of that report's series rather than from inside it. This record reported the opposite on Oct. 20 and the correction is below. The report's numbering does not follow its filing dates: cases numbered 4FA-26-02118CR and 4FA-26-02121CR were filed on Oct. 16 while cases numbered 4FA-26-02109CR to 4FA-26-02117CR were filed on Oct. 18. A count from this report is a minimum for its whole window and not only for its last day.

The report carries no filings for Monday, Oct. 19 at all. That is the second consecutive report whose window covers Monday and which lists nothing filed at Fairbanks that day. Court offices were closed on Oct. 19 for the Alaska Day observance.

The two Delta Junction cases are unchanged: 4DJ-26-00064CR, in which no charging document has yet been filed, and 4DJ-26-00065CR, charging one count of permitting an unauthorised person to drive, an unclassified misdemeanour.

The offence-location column was read separately across all 68 pages. Fairbanks appears on 53 charge lines, North Pole on 11 and Delta Junction on one. No case filed at any other courthouse in this window records an offence location inside the Fairbanks area.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, criminal charges filed

entries.title: Nenana case carries an indicted first-degree burglary charge, a Class B felony, for an offence recorded in Denali National Park
body: Case 4NE-26-00096CR, filed at the Nenana court on Sep. 26, carries six counts against the defendant whose three Nenana cases were reported on Oct. 20. The charge list served by the public case database shows five counts and loads the sixth only on request; all six were read on Oct. 21.

The counts, all with an offence date of Sep. 25 and none flagged as domestic-violence related, are: burglary in the first degree in a dwelling, a Class B felony, with an offence location recorded as Denali National Park; criminal trespass in the first degree in a dwelling, a Class A misdemeanour, Denali National Park; criminal trespass in the first degree on land with intent to commit a crime, a Class A misdemeanour, Denali National Park; theft in the fourth degree, a Class B misdemeanour, Cantwell; and two counts of violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, both Class B misdemeanours, both Cantwell.

The burglary count records an original charge of burglary in the second degree, a Class C felony, and an indicted charge of burglary in the first degree, a Class B felony. An indictment is a charging decision and not a finding.
A competency hearing is set for Nov. 13 at 11 a.m. in Courtroom 402, a calendar call for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30. A motion hearing was held on Oct. 20.

She is charged, not convicted. No victim is identified. Three of the six counts record an offence location of Cantwell, which is outside the Fairbanks area; the park's entrance sits next to Healy, and the park itself extends far beyond the area this record covers.

entries.title: Nenana case charges three Class C felony assault counts for an offence recorded at Fairbanks
body: Case 4NE-26-00103CR, filed at the Nenana court on Oct. 10, charges Ashley with six counts, all with an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Oct. 9, and none flagged as domestic-violence related. The public case database serves five of the six and loads the last on request; all six were read on Oct. 21.

The counts are three of assault in the third degree - repeat threat of death or injury, each a Class C felony; one of driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, a Class A misdemeanour; one of assault in the fourth degree - cause fear of injury, a Class A misdemeanour; and one of driving with a licence cancelled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offence, a Class A misdemeanour.

No indicted charge is recorded against any count, so the case stands on a complaint. An arraignment set for Oct. 20 is recorded as calendared in error and the preliminary hearing for that day as vacated. A new arraignment is set for Oct. 28.
He is charged, not convicted. No victim is identified.

entries.title: Nenana case on an indicted felony drink-driving charge arraigned at Fairbanks
body: Case 4NE-26-00095CR, filed at the Nenana court on Sep. 25, charges Hansen with felony driving under the influence with two or more prior convictions, a Class C felony, and driving with a licence cancelled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offence, a Class A misdemeanour. Both counts record an offence location of Denali National Park and an offence date of Sep. 24, and neither is flagged as domestic-violence related. An indicted charge is recorded against the felony count.

An arraignment is set for 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 in Courtroom 402 at the Fairbanks courthouse. A bail hearing is set for Oct. 22 at 10:15 a.m. following an application for a first bail review filed by the defence on Oct. 20. A calendar call is set for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30.
An arraignment was held on Sep. 25 and preliminary hearings on Oct. 5 and Oct. 15.
She is charged, not convicted. The case appears in no weekly filings report this record has read; the Nenana court has had no section in that report for 25 consecutive weeks.

entries.title: Sixty-four criminal cases on the Fairbanks court calendar, four of them filed at Delta Junction
body: The Fairbanks daily public calendar for Wednesday, Oct. 21, run at 12:02 a.m., lists 64 distinct criminal case numbers over 18 pages. The alphabetical list printed from the same run lists the same 64 numbers.
Fifty-six were filed at the Fairbanks courthouse, four at Delta Junction, one at Nenana and three at courts outside the Fairbanks area. No case filed at Healy appears.

The four Delta Junction cases are 4DJ-26-00045CR, a trial status hearing at 10:30 a.m.; 4DJ-26-00053CR and 4DJ-26-00062CR, both against the same defendant, pre-trial conferences at 10:30 a.m.; and 4DJ-26-00054CR, an arraignment at 1:30 p.m.
Also listed is a bail hearing at 9:15 a.m. in case 4FA-26-01818CR, on a proposed third-party custodian, which was set on Oct. 20 when the hearing scheduled for that day was continued.
The calendar is run once at midnight and lists what is scheduled rather than what happened. No outcome from today's hearings is reported here.

entries.title: Fire crews called to a downtown Fairbanks building fire and to eight traffic collisions
body: The Fairbanks Emergency Communications Center dispatch feed records 44 incidents over roughly the 24 hours to 3:44 a.m. on Oct. 21, of which eight were traffic collisions and two were fires.

A fire at 330 Third Avenue, Suite 315, in Fairbanks was dispatched at 11:08 p.m. on Oct. 20 and closed after one hour and two minutes. A second fire, at Chena Hot Springs Road and Roberts Roost Road, was closed after one minute. An elevator rescue at 1850 Hoselton Road was closed after 13 minutes.

The collisions included two at Lakloey Drive and Badger Road within four minutes of each other, two on the Alaska Route 2 corridor, and one each at the Richardson Highway ramp from the Mitchell Expressway, at Twenty-Second Avenue and Lathrop Street, at Seventh Avenue and Barnette Street, and one still active at milepost 400 of the Elliott Highway.

The feed carries no police or crime incident type and nothing here is reported as a crime. No police, trooper or court record read on Oct. 21 refers to any of these calls. Medical calls on the feed are not reported.

filings.note: The counts by court are the report's own for its own window and are a minimum. The report lists no filings for Monday, Oct. 19, the second consecutive report whose window covers that day. Four cases filed on Oct. 16 and Oct. 17 that were absent from the previous report appear in this one.
